_comment: Reviewed input to scripts/skill_refs.py, the check that the agent-facing instructions
still point at things that exist.
not_paths: references that look like repository paths and deliberately are not. Each
names the file it is in and why. An entry (or one of its refs) that no longer excuses a
failing reference fails the check, so this list cannot outlive what it excuses. Keep it
small: a real path that moved is fixed in the doc, never listed here. Paths git ignores
(build outputs such as backend/.coverage, a local .env) need no entry: they are counted
septacore.subcommands: what `septacore <sub>` may name. Pinned rather than read live,
because CI does not install septacore (it is the operator's harness), and a check that
needs it would be SKIPPED on every CI run. Where septacore is on PATH its --help is read
and a pinned name it no longer lists fails; a new one it lists is a note.

not_paths.reason: A model-id prefix the skill names in order to say it does not exist.
Where gnomon's skill tool writes a proposal; the directory exists only once one has been proposed and not yet accepted.
A file in gnomon's repository (the harness), cited for what it was measured against; not this repository's packages/.
A hypothetical script, the example of what a default verify command could run destructively.
